neighbours.label: ' Europe' as a region name after a compass word (southern / western / northern Europe); weaker on ' European' in institution names
fire: Olive trees grow wild across the Mediterranean basin, from southern Europe to the hills of Lebanon.
The beetle has spread through much of southern Europe, from Portugal to the Greek islands.
Wolves had almost vanished from western Europe by the end of the nineteenth century.
The storm brought heavy snow to northern Europe and closed ports along the Baltic.
Cork oak forests are typical of south-western Europe, especially Spain and Portugal.
Roman roads once linked the towns of southern Europe with the garrisons on the Rhine.
The heatwave moved north from Africa into southern Europe during the first week of July.
Beech woodland covers large parts of central and eastern Europe below the tree line.
quiet: Mangrove trees grow wild across the Indian Ocean rim, from southern Asia to the coast of Kenya.
The beetle has spread through much of southern Africa, from Namibia to the Mozambique coast.
Wolves had almost vanished from western Canada by the end of the nineteenth century.

Inca roads once linked the towns of southern Peru with the forts in the highlands.

Bamboo woodland covers large parts of central and eastern China below the tree line.

notes: Card: ' European' x8, ' Europe' x3, plus a Greek name (Lefteris) and '1'. The + pole's output direction promotes European/EU/Mediterranean tokens, so this pole pushes them down once Europe has been named. Probes: 'southern Europe' 0.53, 'northern Europe' 0.27, 'Western Europe' 0.22, 'European Research Council' 0.22, 'European countries' 0.19, 'several European governments' 0.03; Asia/Canada/Japanese 0.03-0.05. Not a plain token: the same word ranges from 0.03 to 0.53.
